SEMICON Europa 2026 · Exhibition

Controlled environments, built to class.

Every piece of IAQ's corner of the stand, in four variations of one direction: the four stand surfaces, the take-away print, the posts and the ads. Open any piece to see it larger, and download the print files.

WhereMesse München, Munich
When10 to 13 November 2026
The standShared with Green Excel Poland
Hall and standBooth C1 128
See it in 3D
The brief

What the stand has to do.

Goal

Leave European fab owners, EPCM firms and equipment makers knowing one thing: IAQ builds the controlled environment and the whole facility around it, and has a team in Dresden.

Focus

Cleanroom construction, as IAQ asked for the European show. The other two units are named, not explained at length.

Only what is necessary

Only the agreed lines and the published figures: no client names, savings, revenue or projects a client has not cleared.

One action

Every surface points to one action: talk to the team at the counter, or scan the code for the 3D story and the projects.

The direction

The cleanroom, layer by layer.

A white stand drawn in IAQ's isometric: the cleanroom large on the side wall with its four layers named, each with its house icon; the same bay standing tall on the aisle column; one red wall behind the screen, where the three units sit as white line drawings straight on the red. Every take-away piece and post carries the same cleanroom.

Colour, by share of the surface
White, the ground of the stand and of every piece66%
Field red, the wall behind the screen16%
Drawing greys, the isometric drawings9%
Black, statements, names and labels5%
IAQ red, the one red part, one phrase, the line4%
The four layers, named on every piece

Do

  • The cleanroom drawn large, its layers named.
  • One red part in each drawing.
  • The IAQ top left on every piece.
  • One long red line, 400 mm from the floor.

Do not

  • No boxes behind units or labels.
  • No white block on the red wall.
  • No figures beyond the published four.
  • No type on a drawing.
The variations

Variations A to D.

The same direction, the same copy and the same drawings, laid out four ways. Variation D builds on C with IAQ's notes of 8 October, across the stand, the print, the booth screen and the digital. Every piece of each variation is in the sections below, one variation under the other; the 3D views switch between all four. Variations A and B share one set of LinkedIn posts and one email banner; C and D have their own.

AThe exploded cleanroom

  • The cleanroom drawn large with its four layers lifted apart and named, each with its icon.
  • One red wall: the back wall behind the screen, the units drawn white on the red.
  • White aisle column with the tall bay; white leaflet, trifold, roll-up and ads.

BThe cleanroom in three steps

  • The cleanroom going up in three steps: raised floor, wall panels, fan filter units.
  • White side and back walls; the aisle column field red with the bay drawn white.
  • Field red leaflet back, trifold cover and web ads; the roll-up stacks the three steps.

CThe fab in 3D

  • Refined with IAQ's comments of 7 Oct.
  • Side wall: the fab in 3D, its layers led out to three disciplines, each with its services.
  • Back wall: the world with a flag on each office country, our four services and the industries we serve.
  • Aisle column with the six services, plus an option with the tagline; a counter without 3D, with a lead QR and the LinkedIn QR.

DFrom C, IAQ's notes of 8 Oct

  • Every piece: the stand, print, booth screen, LinkedIn posts, web ads and email banner.
  • Side wall: the plain cleanroom in five floors, EPC and PCU & TTI in IAQ's BIM views, and the six-service life cycle across the foot.
  • Back wall: Engineering Today. Advancing Tomorrow., the offices on the map, and a timeline from the founding in Shah Alam in 1995, through France, Sweden and Germany, to SEMICON Europa 2026; the industries on the aisle column.
  • Booth screen: a live website, the fab built floor by floor.

The stand

Four surfaces, at one scale.

From the left: aisle column, side wall, back wall (1736 mm visible of 2046 mm), counter front. Heights from the floor follow berrylife's zones: the IAQ at 3130 to 3340 mm, the statement at 2750 to 3050 mm, the long red line at 400 mm. Variations A to D, one under the other.

Print, to take away

Leaflet, trifold and roll-up.

The PDFs are at trim size with the drawings in vector. The roll-up is for after Munich: the office, site entrances and smaller shows. Variations A to D, one under the other.

Screen and digital

The booth screen, the posts, the ads and the banner.

The 55 inch screen runs a live website; below it, 1080 × 1350 px posts with the agreed captions, and ads at their size, exported at 1x and 2x.

What the 55 inch screen on the back wall shows, running here as it will on the stand. Six chapters loop by themselves: the opening, the fab built floor by floor, the disciplines, IAQ's six-service life cycle, tool hook-up in four phases, and the offices from Shah Alam to Dresden. Any touch hands it to the visitor; a minute untouched and it loops again. Book a meeting opens the two QR codes and the contacts.

Keys: 1 to 6 for a chapter, the arrows, Space to pause, F for full screen.

The booth screen as video

For a media player on the 55 inch screen: the full loop, set to repeat, or one chapter at a time. 1920 × 1080, 30 fps, MP4, silent.

The booth screen, chapter by chapter

One still per chapter, to download: 1920 × 1080 for the screen, 3840 × 2160 for 4K.
